Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Identify needs
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The 'Production and Dissemination Specialist' (EC-05) is responsible for investigating client requirements for statistical information, defining project objectives and priorities, and determining sources of data for special requests (e.g., 'Investigates client requirements for statistical information, defines the nature and scope of special studies, determines the sources of data for special requests as well as the methods and approaches to be used.'). This includes modifying existing techniques or developing new approaches to meet specific needs, integrating data from various sources, and providing expert advice to users inside and outside the organization. Future GSBPM expectation: The future state of 'Identify needs' demands that staff proactively scan all existing data holdings and alternative data sources first, and employ rigorous cost-benefit, timeliness, and risk assessments before initiating any new data collections or surveys. There is an explicit expectation for solution-oriented thinking, automation, reuse, and documentation to support digital workflows, with new data collection being a last resort, justified only as necessary. Role evolution: The EC-05 role will need to evolve from responding to client needs with a survey-first or special study mindset, toward leading a thorough digital/data asset discovery, leveraging internal and external data, and systematically validating if a new collection is required. Decision-making will become more evidence-based, documented, and digitally traceable, with a requirement to challenge default assumptions and construct robust business cases for new surveys. Earlier and more formalized stakeholder engagement will include feasibility, automation, and AI considerations. Capability implication: Greater importance will be placed on in-depth knowledge of data sources (internal, administrative, external), digital navigation skills for metadata-assisted data discovery, the ability to conduct and document cost-benefit-risk analyses, an understanding of automation and AI readiness, and the capability to communicate and justify complex, resource-driven decisions to both clients and internal governance.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Consult and confirm needs
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist is responsible for investigating client requirements for statistical information, defining the nature and scope of special studies, and determining sources of data for special requests and studies. As per the work description, they 'provide subject-matter expertise and consultative services to users within and outside STC' and 'knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for complex statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide advice on program results.' These responsibilities inherently include the consultation and confirmation of stakeholder needs and translating these into statistical products.

Future GSBPM expectation: The future-state for consulting and confirming needs shifts from a focus on initiating new data collection to a model in which existing and alternative data holdings are examined first, leveraging AI-supported platforms and automated discovery tools. Consultations will be more rapid, iterative, outcome-driven, and will emphasize transparent assessment of trade-offs, value, and reusability, with new survey launches being a last resort following explicit, documented justification and cost-benefit analysis.

Role evolution: The EC-05 role will shift from lengthy, exploratory consultations toward facilitating joint assessments of user needs via digital platforms that highlight available holdings and trade-offs. Rather than defaulting to proposing special studies and custom surveys, the specialist will guide stakeholders through the possibilities and limitations of what can be delivered from current assets, using shared metadata and automated tools to evaluate feasibility, timeliness, and value. The role will also require structured documentation and explanation of decision pathways, rationale for rejecting new survey initiation, and negotiation based on the organization’s prioritization criteria. Interactions with clients will be more frequent, agile, and will require real-time, data-driven dialogue.

Capability implication: The new emphasis on data discovery and automated consultation platforms demands much deeper knowledge of agency data holdings, advanced facility with digital data discovery and metadata tools, and fluency in facilitating transparent discussions around data quality, fitness-for-use, value trade-offs, and cost-benefit within fast-paced, outcome-focused cycles. A greater understanding of automated decision support systems, AI-augmented discovery tools, and the rationale for prioritization based on organizational strategy will become vital for effective performance in the redefined consultation process.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Establish output objectives
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist plays a critical role in defining project objectives and priorities, preparing work plans outlining approaches, timeframes, and resources, and determining sources of data for special requests or studies. This includes deciding whether to use existing data sources or to initiate new collection efforts (see: 'Investigates client requirements for statistical information, defines the nature and scope of special studies, determines the sources of data for special requests as well as the methods and approaches to be used.'). The Specialist also interprets user needs, integrates data from various sources, and negotiates with system specialists, methodologists, and clients regarding resources, timeframes, and costs.

Future GSBPM expectation: In the future state, establishing output objectives will require defaulting to the reuse of existing data holdings and demonstrating the infeasibility of meeting needs through alternative or administrative data before proposing new survey activity. Objectives must also embed automation, machine-readability, and interoperability as standard requirements, with explicit digital execution constraints in place from the outset. Resource discipline and a justification-based approach to any manual or custom methods are now front-loaded in the acceptance of objectives.

Role evolution: The EC-05 will need to shift from responding flexibly to client or user needs with bespoke or survey-based solutions, to proactively justifying all proposed data sources and methods within the context of digital-first, automation-enabled, and resource-efficient workflows. The role's responsibility for defining project objectives will be more tightly intertwined with demonstrating compliance with agency-wide automation, interoperability, and reuse criteria, requiring more structured evidence and documentation, and more direct collaboration with IT and data governance experts upfront. The determination of data sources and methods now involves systematic assessment of digital and operational feasibility, not just subject-matter relevance.

Capability implication: As a result, this role will increasingly depend on deep knowledge of internal data assets and agency data architecture, applied understanding of automation and interoperability requirements for output design, digital evaluation techniques, and the frameworks for cost-benefit analysis as applied to statistical output scoping in a digital context. Evaluating trade-offs among reuse, automation, survey scope, and digital scalability will become essential to this role's effectiveness.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Identify concepts
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: EC-05 positions investigate client requirements, define study scope, modify or create approaches to address unique needs, and review/approve processing parameters, including 'develops data bases for the provision of time-series information', 'interprets preliminary results', and 'reviews new and revised processing systems and procedures to ensure compatibility with other statistical programs.' Translating data with differing definitions into common concepts is a substantial part of the role.

Future GSBPM expectation: The increased use of digital inventories, automated mapping tools, and rigorous adherence to interoperable, reusable statistical assets modifies how new data needs are met. Rather than manually reconciling new requirements, the EC-05 will review and justify choices in the context of established frameworks, participate in rapid arbitration across program boundaries, and help adapt or escalate needs that diverge from available assets.

Role evolution: The EC-05 will now need to focus on the evaluation, arbitration, and contextual justification where automated or system-suggested concepts do not align with program needs. Operational workflows become more consultative, cross-functional, and driven by alignment pressure, rather than bespoke solution creation for each request.

Capability implication: A deeper grasp of metadata-driven systems, interoperability challenges, and the principles of justification/exception handling in a digital asset environment becomes necessary to fulfill this evolved responsibility.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Check data availability and suitability
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist is charged with investigating client requirements, determining data sources for special requests, defining methodologies for retrieving, integrating, and producing statistical information, and negotiating with internal and external stakeholders (including data suppliers). The work description emphasizes working with data from diverse, sometimes non-traditional sources, and adapting methods where data was collected for other purposes using different definitions ('Often, the data have been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts.'). It also refers to responsibility for establishing and negotiating contracts for projects and discussing data reporting agreements with suppliers.

Future GSBPM expectation: In the future state, initial data source discovery and suitability is automated and prioritized via intelligent, AI-driven systems. The line between internal, administrative, and third-party data sources is blurred, with human experts called in mainly to evaluate complex suitability cases, legal or confidentiality challenges, or to negotiate and manage relationships with new and non-traditional data owners. Proposals for new surveys require strong, system-generated evidence of necessity, and contract/agreement negotiation becomes more pronounced.

Role evolution: The EC-05 specialist's activities shift from primarily manual identification and ad-hoc assessment of potential data sources to curating, interpreting, and resolving suitability and integration issues flagged by automated tools. The role will increasingly focus on interpreting nuanced gaps or challenges not resolved by technology, and leading negotiations or crafting agreements with alternative data suppliers. Their consultative expertise will be leveraged to support evidence-based justifications for any new data collection and to secure access rights consistent with legal and ethical standards for complex sources.

Capability implication: The ability to comprehend and evaluate the output and logic of automated suitability and discovery systems, as well as to provide authoritative input to legal/ethical risk analyses and data access negotiations, is now essential. Detailed understanding of interoperability challenges, metadata structures, and evolving privacy/contractual frameworks will underpin the specialist's consultative authority in the redefined workflow.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Design outputs and dissemination
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Specialist develops databases and data systems for both internal and user-facing information delivery, guides teams involved in data manipulation and dissemination, and provides expert advice to stakeholders. Responsibilities include 'develop[ing] guidelines for the design, evaluation and testing of processing systems and applications,' 'reviewing and approving processing parameters,' and 'ensuring compatibility with other statistical programs.' The role has significant influence on the design, consistency, and standards of data outputs and dissemination procedures, particularly within current, file- and report-based ecosystems.
Future GSBPM expectation: The transformation under StatCan2030 integrates output/dissemination design into core production, necessitating outputs to be machine/actionable, API-accessible, platform-independent, and extensible by default. The focus moves from standardized human-facing products to reusable, automated, and programmatically accessible assets supporting diverse user and agent requirements, including embargo management and advanced metadata linkage.
Role evolution: The Specialist would need to evolve from overseeing static database/report development to designing and implementing output schemas and dissemination frameworks that enable automated, modular data publishing, robust metadata capture, machine-actionability, and layered access rules. Strategic planning would require anticipating reusability, interoperability, and extensibility from the outset, not as an afterthought. Engagement with IT architects, metadata/governance leads, and data privacy/ethics experts increases, reflecting product/platform stewardship rather than ad hoc output fulfillment.
Capability implication: Priority shifts to understanding and applying metadata standards (e.g., for discoverability and interoperability), machine-actionable output principles, automation best practices, and managed disclosure/confidentiality protocols. Platform thinking, systems integration, and the ability to design for programmatic user scenarios become integral, as does the anticipation of future-proofing assets for new consumer types (e.g., AI agents).

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Design variables
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The Specialist develops databases and coordinates teams manipulating, storing, and retrieving statistical data, providing subject-matter expertise, leading system development activities, and resolving complex issues related to data integration and conceptual conflicts. Evidence: 'Develops databases ... as well as data for special studies and requests', 'reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, devises criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies', and 'reviews new and revised processing systems and procedures to ensure compatibility with other statistical programs'.

Future GSBPM expectation: Moving toward standardized, metadata-rich variable design, the Specialist's role extends to overseeing the governance and implementation of enterprise-wide variables, supporting automated, ‘AI-ready’ data structures, and leading the integration of domain standards within and across programs. The role no longer focuses on creating bespoke variables, but on maintaining, curating, and improving reusable, richly described variable libraries and systems.

Role evolution: The Specialist will become accountable for ensuring that variable choices at the design and implementation stages conform to enterprise interoperability standards, overseeing the metadata management for both in-house and repurposed external variables, and leading the integration with centralized repositories. The role pivots from managing unique project-based requirements toward managing the lifecycle and quality of shared standards, supporting end-to-end automation and facilitating data integration at scale.

Capability implication: This reinforces the need for robust knowledge of metadata and variable management frameworks, semantic harmonization, repository interoperability, and the methodologies for supporting programmatic and automated integration of data assets. Understanding how choices in variable management affect automation, analytics, and governance becomes critical.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Design collection
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist is responsible for investigating client requirements, defining project objectives for special studies, determining sources of data, and developing or modifying techniques to meet specific needs—'Investigates client requirements for statistical information, defines the nature and scope of special studies, determines the sources of data for special requests as well as the methods and approaches to be used.' The role includes developing guidelines for system and application design and reviewing approaches and techniques for database and data retrieval package creation, often integrating data from diverse sources such as financial statements, tax files, and administrative sources in addition to surveys.

Future GSBPM expectation: With automated, metadata-driven design and a default preference for alternative data over survey collection, EC-05s will no longer focus on manual, project-specific instrument development or ad hoc solutioning. Instead, their expertise will be required in configuring, validating, and overseeing enterprise collection frameworks and ensuring the compliant integration of new data sources. The emphasis moves from solving individual project collection needs to systematizing and monitoring collection logic and platform effectiveness across subject-matter domains.

Role evolution: The work moves from hands-on creation and troubleshooting of data collection tools and systems to higher-level stewardship of framework configuration, curation of standardized question banks or data integration points, and exception handling in automated, AI-driven processes. The role will also require greater involvement in cross-functional initiatives to align subject-matter frameworks with interoperable and machine-actionable standards, acting as a bridge between content experts, IT and metadata architects, and AI automation supervisors. Leadership and decision-making shifts from tactical to strategic, with emphasis on monitoring, governance, and adaptability across multiple, reusable systems.

Capability implication: The position will need deeper familiarity with metadata frameworks, automated workflow oversight, enterprise architecture concepts, real-time validation of AI-driven outputs, and the co-creation of ethical, standardized collection methodologies. The role becomes more about steering evolving technologies and platforms to sustain quality and relevancy than about direct instrument-by-instrument design.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Design frame and sample
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist leads teams in developing statistical processing systems, determines data sources for special requests and studies, and reviews and approves the methods and criteria used for manipulations such as sampling frames and data integration from surveys and alternative sources. Notably, they are described as reviewing integration of data 'from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses),' and devising 'criteria and methods' for data consistency and compatibility, which encompasses legacy, manually designed frame and sample construction. Future GSBPM expectation: The transformation to automation shifts the role toward interpreting and approving automatically generated frame/sample designs, guiding how administrative or alternative data are pulled into modular systems, and resolving ambiguous sampling problems flagged by AI or automated systems. Role evolution: This specialist will direct less manual design work and more oversight of automated systems, validate AI-generated sample/frame choices for appropriateness, and ensure standards compliance, focusing on exception handling, systemic improvement of automation, and high-level system integration. Capability implication: Deep knowledge of automated statistical infrastructure becomes critical along with the ability to interpret and defend automated frame/sample selections, assure quality control with cross-domain interoperability, and understand the implications of integrating both legacy and new data sources into sampling automation.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Design processing and analysis
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist oversees the development and coordination of database design, leads teams creating or adapting processing systems, sets and approves detailed processing parameters, and develops guidelines for system design, evaluation and testing. The position involves significant decision-making and integration of new data sources and methods into established processes, as well as ensuring compatibility and continuity across multiple data domains. Future GSBPM expectation: The future state requires the shift of design activity from customizing and documenting individual systems and parameters toward embedding standardized, modular, and automated logic that supports reproducibility, interoperability, and seamless cross-program adaptation. This work will now demand anticipation of system-level automation, event-driven deployment, privacy and audit controls, and the need for rapid integration of varied data sources—moving away from manual configuration and documentation. Role evolution: The EC-05 role will need to prioritize designing, implementing, and reviewing metadata-driven, automation-ready workflows, and orchestrating modules so they can be repurposed with minimal manual change. The focus will be on the management of standardized templates and logic, championing reusability and system interoperability rather than one-off solutions. Capability implication: Proficiency in system configuration for automation, understanding of interoperable design standards, auditability, version control, FAIR data principles, and orchestration of automated workflows will become increasingly central. Deep collaborative and systems thinking will be needed to connect subject-matter needs to machine-actionable, platform-ready specifications and processes.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Design production systems and workflows
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The 'Production and Dissemination Specialist' (EC-05) 'develops databases for the provision of time-series information,' 'reviews and approves detailed processing parameters,' 'develops guidelines for the design, evaluation and testing of processing systems and applications,' and 'leads project teams in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.' The position is responsible for integrating data from multiple sources, resolving technical problems in manipulation and retrieval, and approving system parameters to ensure consistency and quality.

Future GSBPM expectation: The new requirement is for production system design that is modular, reusable, metadata-driven, and highly automated at enterprise scale. Rather than focusing only on ensuring compatibility and integration at the program level, the role will need to oversee or approve the use of standardized, event-driven components that fit within an enterprise-wide workflow orchestration framework.

Role evolution: The EC-05 Specialist's duties will be less about hands-on approval of customized system parameters for each project, and more about setting and enforcing enterprise-aligned design principles, selecting and integrating reusable modules, and ensuring that all production processes are auditable, version-controlled, and support rapid adaptation. The Specialist must facilitate team adoption of automation and self-service (by non-technical staff), manage the interface between business requirements and standardized technical building blocks, and ensure compliance with enterprise architecture and governance practices.

Capability implication: Comprehensive knowledge of enterprise workflow orchestration, modular architecture, event-driven automation, metadata-driven processes, and governance/guardrail frameworks becomes increasingly foundational. The ability to translate business and subject-matter requirements into specifications usable in modular or low-code environments, as well as understanding cross-program implications of workflow changes and how to enable horizontal reuse, are new critical domains of expertise.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Reuse or build collection instruments
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist manages database design and development, supervises staff activities related to data manipulation and retrieval, represents subject-matter divisions in projects, and provides advice on statistical concepts and procedural developments. The role includes responsibility for designing and reviewing system specifications and for reconciling technical, procedural, and subject-matter issues across a program.
Future GSBPM expectation: Instrument creation and maintenance will now occur using corporate, modular, self-service platforms. This shifts responsibility from custom-building or extensively modifying instruments and processes to ensuring that platforms are correctly assembled from standardized components, are interoperable through metadata, and support audit and paradata capabilities by default.
Role evolution: The specialist will need to pivot from procedural expertise in ad hoc or traditionally-coded solutions to assuring the effectiveness, compliance, and operational fit of modular and automated workflows. They will need to lead teams in configuring these environments, evaluate and troubleshoot automated extraction and instrument routines, and provide consultative oversight as subject-matter staff across the organization increasingly directly create or configure collection instruments.
Capability implication: This raises the bar for capabilities in modular system governance, operational monitoring of AI-driven or no-code/low-code environments, application of digital guardrails to ensure compliance, and management/interpretation of metadata linking instrument design, deployment, and paradata for program and organizational oversight.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist leads projects and teams for the development and implementation of processing systems, resolves technical problems in data manipulation/storage/retrieval, and develops guidelines for processing system design and evaluation. Key duties include 'Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.'

Future GSBPM expectation: As processing and analysis tooling becomes composable and standardized, this role will be responsible for ensuring that new and existing systems leverage reusable, automated components, and for guaranteeing rigorous compliance with new expectations for auditability, orchestration, reproducibility, and secure pipeline management.

Role evolution: Activities shift from steering custom-built system projects toward managing the assembly of microservices and AI-enabled components within controlled platforms, reviewing modular workflow integration, and overseeing compliance with reproducibility and security requirements across diverse subject areas.

Capability implication: There will be heightened importance of understanding enterprise component libraries, oversight of automated orchestration environments, evaluation of module compatibility, and expertise in workflow documentation and compliance—a shift from development to stewardship of composable analytical ecosystems.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Reuse or build dissemination components
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist leads teams in developing processing systems, advises users, and is responsible for establishing and applying standards and procedures for dissemination, including 'develops guidelines for the design, evaluation and testing of processing systems and applications,' and reviews and approves new or revised processing systems. They must ensure compatibility with other programs, advise on departmental publication, marketing, and dissemination policies, and ensure compliance with security and confidentiality standards. Future GSBPM expectation: StatCan2030 directs a move away from siloed or locally-defined guidelines and platforms, requiring all dissemination to be based on reusable, standardized, and modular solutions implemented on enterprise-managed toolkits with automation and AI-readiness as defaults. Role evolution: The Specialist will need to replace any practices or guidelines oriented toward custom or locally-managed systems with expertise in configuring, validating, and improving dissemination outputs within the set of enterprise-sanctioned platforms. The function shifts from approving and developing standalone parameters toward ensuring all dissemination activities comply with modularization, standardization, and governance requirements, and actively collaborating across technical and subject-matter boundaries to ensure reusable outputs. The Specialist's consultative function extends to navigating platform guardrails and translating advanced user needs into standardized, interoperable configurations. Capability implication: Key capabilities will include understanding of automation and workflow orchestration within enterprise platforms, metadata-driven design, and AI/machine-oriented dissemination standards. It also heightens the importance of being proficient in integrating local requirements into standardized, reusable corporate solutions rather than customizing from the ground up.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Configure workflows
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist develops databases, coordinates teams manipulating/storing data, and oversees the design, evaluation, and testing of processing systems ('Develops guidelines for the design, evaluation and testing of processing systems and applications and recommends modifications and improvements to existing procedures.'). The EC-05 leads teams in the development and implementation of new or modified processing systems and resolves technical and conceptual problems to ensure data quality and compatibility.

Future GSBPM expectation: Workflow configuration in the future state requires use of standardized, modular orchestration platforms driving automation, transparency, and audibility. The expectation is for business lines, under the leadership of senior technical specialists, to adapt and configure workflows through low-code/no-code platforms in direct partnership with IT governance, and to ensure all changes are versioned and compliant.

Role evolution: The EC-05 will move from managing and tweaking local systems and procedures in an ad hoc manner toward designing, assembling, and maintaining automated, versioned workflows using shared platforms. Operational oversight will include governance of standardized workflow modules, troubleshooting and adapting enterprise solutions rather than building one-off solutions, and ensuring business needs are met while adhering to enterprise standards for configuration, transparency, and traceability.

Capability implication: The role will require applied knowledge of orchestration platforms, automated workflow lifecycle management, and governance mechanisms for change. Understanding the interface between business requirements and IT guardrails—especially with regards to self-service tools, modularity, and audit trails—will be more important, reinforcing the need to navigate a hybrid technical/business orchestration environment.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Test production systems
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist develops guidelines for the design, evaluation, and testing of processing systems and applications and recommends improvements to existing procedures. The position also reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, devises criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies, and designs and creates test procedures and acceptance criteria. Evidence: 'Develops guidelines for the design, evaluation and testing of processing systems and applications and recommends modifications and improvements to existing procedures.' and 'Research and analysis are required to evaluate the effectiveness of processing systems, to formulate computer systems specifications, to design and create test procedures and acceptance criteria.'
Future GSBPM expectation: The organization requires testing to be automated, continuous, and embedded within modular and self-service production systems, with a focus on not only functional correctness but also auditability, compliance (security, privacy, reproducibility), and enterprise-wide standards within orchestrated workflows.
Role evolution: The specialist’s responsibilities will expand to include the development and stewardship of comprehensive, automated, and reproducible testing frameworks; ensuring compliance checks (security, privacy, audit) are built into the testing and deployment pipelines; and attesting to compliance readiness for automated approvals. The specialist will serve as a bridge between business requirements, technical implementation, and governance constraints.
Capability implication: Expertise in regulatory and audit controls for data production, orchestration of automated testing within modular and self-service environments, integration of compliance protocols, and systemized documentation practices will be increasingly necessary.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Test statistical business process
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The Production and Dissemination Specialist (EC-05) currently develops guidelines for the design, evaluation, and testing of processing systems and applications, and recommends modifications to improve procedures. The role involves reviewing and approving processing parameters, devising criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies, and developing specifications for data compilation programs. Evidence: 'Develops guidelines for the design, evaluation and testing of processing systems and applications' and 'Research and analysis are required to...design and create test procedures and acceptance criteria to ensure that processing systems yield the desired outputs.'
Future GSBPM expectation: Modernization of GSBPM 3.6 will require more formalized, transparent, and comprehensive testing strategies that go beyond system-focused testing towards business process validation, addressing test coverage for changes affecting input, transformation logic, workflow dependencies, and output/quality.
Role evolution: The role’s activities would evolve to include a stronger emphasis on the orchestration, documentation, and continual improvement of test frameworks and acceptance criteria across the business process. There will be greater requirement for oversight of multi-disciplinary testing—including, for example, dealing with automation pipelines, version management, and test result traceability in collaboration with IT and methodology specialists.
Capability implication: Specialist knowledge will be needed in test architecture for modular and complex statistical systems, change impact assessment, and the translation of process requirements into test plans that fully assure the statistical process's fitness-for-purpose—and that effectively support rapid iteration and innovation.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Finalise production systems
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: 1. Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist leads teams in the development and implementation of processing systems and databases, approves processing parameters, ensures compatibility with other statistical programs, and develops guidelines for system design and evaluation ('Leads project teams ... in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems,' 'Develops guidelines for the design, evaluation and testing of processing systems and applications...'). There is a strong emphasis on system integration, data consistency, system testing, and advisory support for users. 2. Future GSBPM expectation: In the future state, the finalisation of production systems incorporates operationalization of automated, AI-enabled workflows, robust versioning, compliance checks (security, FAIR), broad documentation, and role-based training to empower non-technical users. The shift to rapid, self-serve, modular platforms means production finalization is ongoing, not a single event, and spans both monitoring and facilitating empowered use by business staff. 3. Role evolution: This position’s coordination and system integration expertise will need to evolve toward operationalizing and attesting to modular, automated pipelines, embedding compliance, facilitating role-based documentation, and ongoing enablement. The role expands from technical development to governance and shared monitoring, including supporting users across subject-matter and analytics teams. The specialist will be a key actor in ensuring production systems’ functionality, adaptability, and compliance are not only technically complete but also organizationally sustainable and transparent. 4. Capability implication: Ownership of and accountability for system finalization means increased importance of knowledge around system modularity, automation frameworks, documentation practices for diverse audiences, and compliance with security/reproducibility standards. The ability to lead cross-functional teams in actively governing and enabling production systems for dynamic adjustment and rapid deployment will be essential.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Create frame and select sample – Future-State Implications
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist leads teams responsible for developing databases and statistical processing systems, and approves parameters or develops new methods for integrating and retrieving statistical data. This includes providing subject-matter services, often dealing with multiple data sources for studies and projects. Decision-making responsibilities include reviewing and approving processing parameters, developing guidelines for processing systems, and evaluating the impact of technological developments on procedural approaches. Domains often include integration of alternative or non-survey data sources.

Future GSBPM expectation: As automated processes govern most of sampling and frame-building, the EC-05 will play an essential role in specifying, validating, and continuously improving these automated workflows, overseeing the blending of auxiliary information into frames, and managing complex, rare exceptions. The focus will be on supporting the platform logic for harmonization and burden management in scalable, auditable workflows.

Role evolution: The EC-05 will transition from directly coordinating manual or semi-manual statistical production activities to providing oversight, assurance, and innovation within automated, cross-program sampling/frames platforms. Their work will deeply involve auditing the efficacy of these automation approaches, evaluating exception handling, and integrating new sources to maximize frame coverage.

Capability implication: Increased emphasis will fall on expert knowledge of automated sampling logic, automated quality assurance design, and process transparency, along with the expertise required to harmonize frames and samples across programs. The need to interpret, monitor, and improve AI-augmented modules and manage data integrity and exception processes across enterprise platforms becomes a core responsibility.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Set up collection
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist plans, develops, and approves processing system parameters, integration of varied data sources, and leads project teams implementing new/modified processing systems ('Develops guidelines for the design, evaluation and testing of processing systems and applications and recommends modifications and improvements to existing procedures.' and 'Coordinates and controls the activities of staff involved in manipulating, storing and retrieving statistical data.'). They are also responsible for managing activities around complex system improvements, technical integration for special studies, and evaluating the impact of technological developments. 
Future GSBPM expectation: Collection set-up in the future will be predominantly automated with human oversight focusing on risk/quality monitoring, exception handling, and assurance of compliance (including privacy and security management in pre-built modules). System and process customizations become rare; adaptation comes via modular, reusable templates and platforms, with rapid cycles and extensive use of automation. 
Role evolution: This specialist will shift from individually tailoring systems for each need or study to overseeing and validating automated platform outputs, monitoring risk and exception reports, requesting new templates or platform modules as needs arise, and reviewing AI-driven logic for bias, compliance, and reliability. Leadership emphasis moves towards ensuring operational integrity and continuity using these new approaches, and collaborating on enterprise-wide system design and governance, rather than championing custom-built flows. 
Capability implication: Deep knowledge of statistical production automation, data integration from non-survey and new digital sources, AI-driven process governance, and compliance embedded within modular solution architectures becomes far more consequential.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Run collection
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Specialist leads teams in the development and oversight of data production processes, integrating data from various sources, and devising new approaches for producing statistical outputs ('Coordinates and controls the activities of staff involved in manipulating, storing and retrieving statistical data.'; 'Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.'). They interpret client requirements, select appropriate data sources, and adapt approaches to provide integrated statistical information. Their analytical work often involves evaluating and improving existing processing systems.

Future GSBPM expectation: With 'Run collection' shifting to automated, highly orchestrated pipelines, the EC-05 Specialist’s responsibility will move from managing staff performing routine manual or semi-automated collection towards leading teams focused on oversight, optimization, and adaptation of the automated end-to-end data acquisition environment. Manual respondent interaction is an exception; their leadership will involve ensuring digital workflows function correctly, troubleshooting rare or complex failures, and refining integration with a broader variety of administrative and alternative data sources via digital interfaces.

Role evolution: The EC-05 will be responsible for ensuring overall operational reliability of the collection pipeline, integrating new data sources, and supporting cross-functional team management in a context where process reengineering and system resilience are priorities over direct management of traditional collection activities. Leadership will mean guiding staff through interpretative, quality-focused interventions within the automated environment, drawing on digital paradata and monitoring insights, and adapting strategies as new technologies and data sources are onboarded.

Capability implication: Deep understanding of how to operationalize and manage automated, multi-source data collection pipelines, expertise in digital monitoring and exception-handling environments, and the ability to connect technical system insights (e.g., process performance, paradata) to program objectives and methodological imperatives become increasingly important in this role.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Finalise collection
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Specialist develops and manages databases, supervises work on manipulating, storing, retrieving data, and leads the development and implementation of new statistical processing systems ('Develops data bases for the provision of time-series information as well as data for special studies and requests.'; 'Coordinates and controls the activities of staff involved in manipulating, storing and retrieving statistical data.'). They devise guidelines for processing systems and adapt methods to ensure data quality and compatibility, frequently overseeing a blend of manual routines, ad hoc solutions, and incremental system enhancements for data handoff/archiving.
Future GSBPM expectation: The transition to automated, standardized, and metadata-intensive finalization processes removes most manual interaction with collected data. The Specialist will no longer focus on organizing or guiding manual workflows for data handoff, archiving, or transformation; instead, oversight shifts to monitoring, designing, and continuously improving the automated collection-to-processing interface and exception pathways. Ensuring all data instruments and versions are discoverable and archived in machine-actionable ways becomes default, with privacy/pseudonymization embedded.
Role evolution: The Specialist will pivot to establishing and refining orchestration logic, collaborating on pipeline and metadata repository design, and ensuring exception handling is robust and well-instrumented. Assessments of quality and process effectiveness must rely increasingly on paradata, audit trails, and system metrics—not manual inspection. Oversight of automation (including incident and exception triaging) grows central, while detailed manual data curation, archiving, or editing becomes obsolete.
Capability implication: Strong practical knowledge in pipeline-based automation, data/metadata modeling, orchestration, real-time quality metric assessment, and exception management becomes vital. The Specialist’s consultative role extends to evaluating and improving metadata and workflow automation to ensure data is discoverable, reusable, and auditable by design, shifting the focus to continuous process and automation improvement rather than manual data management.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Integrate data
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist coordinates and controls the manipulation, storage, and retrieval of statistical data and leads teams implementing new or improved processing systems. The work involves integrating data from various sources, developing databases for special studies, and ensuring consistency through coding systems and processing specifications (e.g., 'Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, devises criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies and recommends modifications to ensure the continuity and compatibility of data,' and 'Some studies may involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources...the data have been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts.'). Future GSBPM expectation: The future state requires streamlined integration using automated, modular components, reducing manual harmonization and increasing the role of metadata, standardized inputs/outputs, and automation in production pipelines. Role evolution: The EC-05 will need to lead and supervise not only teams but also the configuration and validation of end-to-end automated data integration pipelines, focusing on real-time process monitoring, metadata curation, standardization of integration logic, and the governance of automated workflows and exception handling. Capability implication: Greater value will be placed on knowledge of data orchestration platforms, management of reusable integration modules, and the ability to oversee auditable, automated data flows, rather than in-depth manual coding or harmonization. Understanding and stewardship of interoperability and metadata management will become key.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Classify and code
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist oversees databases, leads teams developing processing systems, and provides subject-matter expertise with a high level of accountability for designing processing parameters, approving classification and coding systems, and ensuring operational compatibility with other statistical programs (e.g., 'Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, classification, coding systems and report formats or develops new ones to meet specific needs'). This role involves a holistic and integrative view of how classification and coding fit into the larger data value chain. Future GSBPM expectation: With classification and coding becoming highly automated and managed through central, auditable AI modules, the EC-05's focus migrates from hands-on development and approval of coding systems toward model and metadata governance, exception policy definition, and continuous validation of AI-driven outputs for consistency and quality. They will also be more involved in setting requirements for model retraining and system adaptation in response to changing input data or external requirements. Role evolution: The EC-05 will become key custodians of the evolving classification frameworks, responsible for validating the appropriateness and effectiveness of automated coding methods, overseeing exception and edge case resolution, and coordinating the interplay between automated classification and other subject-matter domains. Capability implication: Deep contextual understanding of cross-domain standardization, AI model performance monitoring, and risk-based exception governance will become central to fulfilling this role. The incumbent must be adept at synthesizing system performance insights, stewarding change management, and ensuring compliance with organization-wide standards and ethical guidelines for automated processing.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: GSBPM 5.3 Review and Validate – Future-State Implications
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Specialist leads or coordinates units involved in manipulating, storing, and especially "retrieving" validated data, developing guidelines for system evaluation and testing, and recommends improvements to existing validation procedures. The role includes "reviews and approves detailed processing parameters," "develops guidelines for the design, evaluation and testing of processing systems," and "reviews new and revised processing systems and procedures to ensure compatibility with other statistical programs," all of which are closely aligned with the review and validation stage.

Future GSBPM expectation: Specialists must guide and ensure the operationalization of automated, scalable, and standardized validation practices, limiting manual interventions to edge-case analysis and quality oversight.

Role evolution: This position will transition from direct review of data and ad hoc process improvements to governance, monitoring, and continuous quality assurance of validation modules and their outputs, as well as oversight of validation exception management and root-cause analysis. EC-05s are likely to lead efforts in adapting subject-matter-driven validation requirements into standard automated rules and monitor validation pipelines for both performance and integrity.

Capability implication: The capacity to “translate” complex subject-matter logic into programmable and auditable rules, lead cross-domain standardization, scrutinize automated validation outcomes, and ensure audit trails will be critical. Understanding process automation, version control of logic, and hybrid governance (AI/human) processes will take on greater importance.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Edit and impute
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 'Production and Dissemination Specialist' leads teams and projects involving the manipulation, storage, and retrieval of statistical data, including the development of guidelines for processing systems, and is responsible for reviewing and approving processing parameters as well as recommending modifications to improve data quality. Evidence is present in 'Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, devises criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies and recommends modifications to ensure the continuity and compatibility of data,' and 'Develops guidelines for the design, evaluation and testing of processing systems and applications.'
Future GSBPM expectation: The future model for edit/impute means these tasks are automated, standardized, and integrated across domains. The EC-05 will thus become a primary actor in defining the oversight mechanisms, criteria, and parameters for automated and AI-driven pipelines, ensuring their outputs match quality, audit, and fairness standards. Their role expands to developing test specifications for modular services, managing complex exceptions/escalations, and advocating changes that align with centralized automation.
Role evolution: EC-05s move from direct supervision of staff doing manual or semi-automated manipulation to leadership of oversight on automated pipelines, exception management, and governance of algorithmic performance. They will be key in cross-program coordination to align automated edits/imputations, monitoring for unintended consequences and leading thorough, documented investigation of pipeline failures, ethical issues, or significant exceptions.
Capability implication: This role will require advanced capabilities in interpreting automation system outputs, governing AI-enabled solutions, and evaluating the quality, explainability, and fairness of algorithmic interventions across programs. EC-05s will increasingly need to understand both the technical and ethical underpinnings of automation, handle complex escalations, and communicate system-level decisions to internal and external audiences confidently.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Derive new variables and units
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist develops and coordinates database and data manipulation activities, leads teams implementing new or modified statistical processing systems, and provides subject-matter expertise to support system improvements. They investigate client requirements, develop new approaches for integrating and preparing data, review and approve processing parameters and coding systems, and recommend procedural enhancements ('Develops guidelines for the design, evaluation and testing of processing systems and applications and recommends modifications and improvements to existing procedures').

Future GSBPM expectation: With statistical derivations embedded in automated, orchestrated microservices, the EC-05 specialist's activities will be less about direct manipulation, and more about formal stewardship over the logic that underpins derivation services. Their focus shifts to designing transformation logic for cross-domain reuse, validating and impacting automated logic, monitoring pipeline outputs, and ensuring compliance with audit, version control, and quality standards. They may also be required to lead the roll-out of new modules or updates across multiple subject-matter areas simultaneously.

Role evolution: The EC-05 will evolve from hands-on operational oversight and tailored solution-building toward a leadership and oversight role in the automation environment. Key ongoing activities include managing the governance and documentation of derivation modules, conducting impact assessments for pipeline changes, leading investigation into exceptions, and ensuring transformation modules meet broad quality and audit expectations.

Capability implication: Advanced capability in the formal logic and documentation of data transformations, stewardship of metadata and standards, understanding modular data pipeline design, and driving compliance and auditability through standardized automated workflows will become central responsibilities.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Calculate weights
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 'Production and Dissemination Specialist' coordinates and controls staff involved in data manipulation, develops guidelines for the design and testing of processing systems, reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, and leads teams in developing and implementing new or modified processing systems ('Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, devises criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies and recommends modifications...'). Future GSBPM expectation: As weight calculation becomes a standardized, automated pipeline step governed by modular architecture and AI-support, responsibility shifts from approving manual routines or direct data manipulation to defining and overseeing the parameters and rules embedded within these automated modules. The EC-05 will also be accountable for ensuring that configuration and exception processes are in place, balancing quality, auditability, and resilience across a broader range of data sources. Role evolution: EC-05 roles will move from supervising and directly reviewing production steps to managing the parameterization and oversight of automated processes, reviewing system performance, and making higher-level determinations about methodology updates or interventions required in rare exceptions. Decisions about weighting strategies and their operational deployment will depend on effective interface with IT, governance mechanisms, and pipeline orchestration systems. Capability implication: Deeper expertise in automation logic, pipeline management, and the governance of AI/machine learning-supported processes becomes crucial. The ability to understand, audit, and explain automated weighting performance and exceptions, and to operationalize conceptual methodological changes into systemized modules, increases in importance.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Calculate aggregates
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Specialist develops databases, coordinates staff engaged in data manipulation and aggregation, leads projects developing or modifying statistical processing systems, and reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, ensuring appropriate methodologies and data transformations. They are tasked with 'developing guidelines for the design, evaluation and testing of processing systems and applications and recommending modifications and improvements,' as well as 'reviewing and approving detailed processing parameters.'

Future GSBPM expectation: As GSBPM 5.7 aggregation shifts to centrally-managed, automated aggregation microservices, these Specialists will be responsible for ensuring that their teams and projects utilize, configure, and validate these standardized components as part of enterprise pipelines. Idiosyncratic or local process variations must be formally justified and approved, and most aggregation tasks will be operationalized via configuration rather than custom programming.

Role evolution: The EC-05 must pivot from hands-on system design and custom parameter definition to managing the use of automated services, overseeing exception management, and verifying compliance with pipeline governance. Their subject-matter expertise will be increasingly applied in configuring aggregation components (e.g., specifying measures or weighting) and in interpreting and defending aggregation outputs in communications. Their leadership is needed in promoting adherence to standard processes and in escalating requirements when existing modules do not suffice.

Capability implication: Familiarity with enterprise configuration management, metadata-driven process controls, and automated validation/reporting will be vital. The role will require a strong ability to assess both process conformity and the business meaning of automated outputs, manage documentation and reproducibility, and lead staff through operational changes, including the handling of exceptions or complex configurations.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Finalise data files
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The Specialist coordinates database development and production activities, leads teams, and devises methods to ensure continuity, compatibility, and reliability of statistical data ('Coordinates and controls the activities of staff involved in manipulating, storing and retrieving statistical data', 'Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters... and recommends modifications to ensure the continuity and compatibility of data'). Much of this work currently requires oversight of manual interventions, process evaluation, and troubleshooting inconsistencies within bespoke or semi-standardized work routines. Future GSBPM expectation: In the future-state, this role shifts from leading and managing manual workflow execution to ensuring that automated, modular pipelines produce reliable, standardized, and machine-actionable data outputs. Emphasis is placed on auditability, versioning, seamless integration with downstream processes, and oversight of exception handling rather than hands-on data manipulation. Role evolution: The EC-05 will be required to manage and certify the operation of automated finalization pipelines, intervene only in complex cases not handled by automation, and assure that programmatic standards are met for all finalized data files. Decision-making will be based on audit trails and exception logs from automated processes rather than direct inspection or correction of output files. Capability implication: Knowledge of metadata standards implementation, automated pipeline management, inspection of system verifications, and understanding compliance frameworks for data traceability and transparency will become pivotal, along with expertise in validating the outputs of autonomous, reproducible production systems.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Prepare draft outputs
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist is responsible for coordinating and controlling data production activities and leading teams involved in producing and disseminating statistical information. Tasks include 'develops guidelines for the design, evaluation and testing of processing systems and applications and recommends modifications and improvements to existing procedures,' and 'reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, devises criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies.' Their work involves decision-making about the technical preparation, evaluation, and compilation of data for outputs such as statistical tables and reports.

Future GSBPM expectation: The future model fundamentally alters the mode of output preparation, using AI-native automation to assemble all but the most complex outputs. Human focus is realigned towards oversight, managing system exceptions, validating pipeline outputs, and interpreting results for customers and the organization.

Role evolution: The EC-05 Specialist will move from overseeing manual or semi-automated compilation and formatting towards managing pipeline configuration, performance, and exception protocols. Their responsibility shifts towards reviewing the efficacy of automated production guidelines and deploying changes to pipeline templates, dashboards, or standard outputs. Furthermore, they will need to use their subject-matter expertise to contextualize and interpret outputs, handle pipeline exceptions, and advise on automation improvements rather than executing manual or discrete technical tasks.

Capability implication: This intensifies the need for expertise in reviewing, diagnosing, and updating automated pipeline systems, ensuring the relevance and accuracy of subject-matter parameters for standardized production, and leading teams in an environment of rapid system-level change and automation.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Validate outputs
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The Specialist leads teams and projects related to developing databases and processing systems, providing subject-matter guidance, and 'develops guidelines for the design, evaluation and testing of processing systems and applications and recommends modifications and improvements to existing procedures.' They are responsible for 'reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, devises criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies,' and ensuring that data quality and consistency is maintained in outputs.
Future GSBPM expectation: The transition to automated, AI-supported output validation pipelines will markedly change how specialists approach quality assurance and error detection, reducing manual review while demanding more sophisticated oversight over automation and greater involvement in validating, updating, and interpreting validation logic and exceptional outputs. 
Role evolution: Specialists will need to shift from personally executing or approving manual validation routines to setting standards for automated validation, developing and regulating AI-driven validation rules, and providing expert interpretation of anomalies or exceptions escalated by the system. They will need to ensure transparency and accountability in automated validation, contribute to root-cause analysis when exceptions are flagged, and provide input to the ongoing development of validation frameworks.
Capability implication: The position will require advanced capabilities in managing and overseeing AI-based quality assurance, understanding how automated validation logic works, determining when and how to intervene, and ensuring that the integrity, transparency, and trustworthiness of output validation processes are maintained.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Interpret and explain outputs
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist leads teams in developing and interpreting data, often integrating and analyzing outputs for complex policy and societal questions ('Provides expert advice and guidance to all levels of government...on statistical program results...', 'Interprets the results of tests, procedural investigations and feasibility studies to produce data bases and data retrieval packages used for the production of integrated statistical information.'). They are also responsible for writing explanatory content and ensuring data is properly contextualized for various audiences. Future GSBPM expectation: In the future, as the technical and routine analytics are automated and pipelines supply complex outputs, the Specialist will focus on higher-order interpretation, narrative development, and ethical stewardship of findings, serving as the 'last mile' bridge to program and policy meaning. They will also have oversight responsibilities for the implementation and human supervision of automated processes, especially related to transparency, quality, and ethical constraints of AI use. Role evolution: Routine work on system development, data processing, and standard summary analysis will recede, while the need to draw societal or policy narratives, articulate limitations, evaluate ethical and quality risks, and maintain trust in automation increases. The specialist will enable and defend the responsible use of statistical outputs in potentially sensitive or high-impact domains. Capability implication: Enhanced importance for advanced analytical reasoning, interpretive judgment, AI oversight knowledge, and frameworks for transparent/ethical communication of results. Deep contextual awareness (including risks and risks of misinterpretation) and sophisticated communicative abilities will be required, alongside proficiency in evaluating the trustworthiness and policy fit of AI-derived data.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Apply disclosure control
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist leads teams involved in manipulating, storing, retrieving, and disseminating statistical data; develops and approves processing parameters; provides subject-matter expertise on statistical methods; and ensures compliance with confidentiality policies: 'Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, data quality), practices and classification systems to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of statistical projects and activities.' Future GSBPM expectation: Disclosure control moves to an automated, standardized, end-to-end pipeline in which the specialist will be expected to oversee the design of disclosure routines, monitor integration within broader analytical workflows, and manage fast, responsive exception handling and auditability. Role evolution: The specialist, now tasked with direct supervision of sensitive data operations and policy compliance, will need to facilitate the orchestration of automated disclosure routines, coordinate redesigns or parameter adjustments in response to new output formats, and supervise the resolution of exceptions that arise from automated decision systems or unusual outputs. This will place increased focus on audit process design, exception management protocols, and alignment between subject-matter, technical, and policy perspectives. Capability implication: Greater emphasis on system-centric oversight, real-time exception response, policy-driven automation stewardship, and the ability to evaluate system-driven confidentiality outputs for accuracy and fairness.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Finalise outputs
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist leads and approves processing systems and databases, reviews and approves parameters, and develops guidelines for design, evaluation, and testing of production systems. The specialist is also responsible for resolving inconsistencies, ensuring output compatibility, and providing subject-matter expertise on dissemination outputs. This includes operational and strategic influence over output finalization approaches (e.g., 'Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, devises criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies and recommends modifications to ensure the continuity and compatibility of data.').
Future GSBPM expectation: In the modernized future state, the specialist’s oversight will be exercised primarily over automated pipelines rather than direct manual review and rectification. EC-05s will be expected to provide strategic guidance on the configuration and continuous improvement of automated approval, caveat assignment, and documentation processes, ensuring these align with agency standards and user needs in a high-throughput environment.
Role evolution: The EC-05 will focus on the governance of automated workflows, reviewing edge cases and outputs flagged by systems, interpreting AI-generated support materials, and making strategic or exceptional sign-off decisions. They will also champion the implementation of systematized documentation, provenance tracking, and reproducibility, and drive improvements in the effectiveness of automation in final output processes.
Capability implication: More importance will be placed on audit/trust in automation, interpretation of AI-generated documentation, and the ability to assess and improve automated processes for quality, reproducibility, and exception handling.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Update output systems
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist is tasked with overseeing databases for time-series information, controlling staff activities related to manipulating/storing/retrieving data, and providing consultative services about output interpretation and dissemination. The role includes developing guidelines for system design, evaluating processing parameters, and ensuring compatibility with departmental publication and dissemination policies, as documented in 'Develops data bases for the provision of time-series information' and 'Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination.' Future GSBPM expectation: Under StatCan2030, producing and disseminating data is centrally automated and metadata-driven, with strict enterprise standards, machine-ready formats, and modular publication components. The role's involvement in manual formatting, selecting publication parameters for human consumption, and operational troubleshooting is de-emphasized, replaced by tasks such as specifying and validating metadata, monitoring system output, and contributing to enterprise oversight of dissemination standards. Role evolution: The specialist will focus on reviewing, curating, and improving metadata to guarantee compliance with FAIR principles and publication standards, and liaising with automation/platform teams to translate subject-matter nuances into machine-actionable outputs. The practical work of operationally coordinating ad-hoc outputs will be supplanted by quality oversight and continuous improvement for system outputs. Capability implication: Profound understanding of FAIR data principles, enterprise metadata management, compliance validation, and the ability to translate complex subject-matter requirements into standardized interoperable outputs are necessary, as is participation in enterprise data governance and exception management.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: GSBPM 7.2 - Produce dissemination products
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The Production and Dissemination Specialist (EC-05) leads database development, coordinates activities related to manipulation and retrieval of data, provides subject-matter expertise, and leads teams for the implementation of processing systems, including responsibility for policies and practices in data preparation and dissemination (e.g., 'Coordinates and controls the activities of staff involved in manipulating, storing and retrieving statistical data'; 'Develops data bases for the provision of time-series information as well as data for special studies and requests').
Future GSBPM expectation: Dissemination will rely on interconnected, modular, and AI-enabled automated pipelines. The EC-05 specialist will focus on managing these infrastructures, guiding staff through exceptions or complex requirements, and driving template/platform evolution to suit emerging dissemination formats (dashboards, APIs, reusable data).
Role evolution: The EC-05’s leadership will focus less on day-to-day operational management of routines and more on championing the transition to automated dissemination, overseeing system enhancements, engaging with cross-functional teams, and ensuring that outputs meet both business and technical standards of quality, accessibility, and reusability. They will have to assess and ensure the dissemination platform’s ability to rapidly generate and publish new product types and handle ad hoc requests efficiently.
Capability implication: The role demands increased expertise in managing modular and automated dissemination infrastructure, the ability to diagnose platform-level issues, and adeptness at quality assurance of outputs across a range of delivery channels (including machine-to-machine).

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Release dissemination products
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 'Production and Dissemination Specialist' develops databases for dissemination, coordinates and controls the activities involved in manipulating, storing and retrieving statistical data, and provides expertise on policy, security, and quality issues in data release. The role involves reviewing and approving processing parameters, resolving inconsistencies, and ensuring compliance with publication and dissemination protocols, including marketing and communications to users. Future GSBPM expectation: As release mechanics become platform-automated, the role will move from operational supervision to oversight of automated dissemination pipelines, with heightened responsibility for policy compliance, auditing, and exception management (such as managing urgent retraction or embargo breach through automated systems). The specialist will be expected to govern and optimize workflows in automated platforms, ensuring outputs are both quality-assured and policy-compliant.
