Role evolution: The role will require increased focus on oversight and intervention only in exceptional cases, setting escalation protocols, and contributing expertise in defining the business rules that platforms follow for secure and auditable releases. Capability implication: More importance will be placed on policy interpretation in an automation context, understanding data workflow orchestration, systemic risk assessment, and exception governance within automated dissemination environments.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Promote dissemination products
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Specialist leads teams, coordinates dissemination, and provides subject matter expertise on statistical program results, including advisement and policy input on dissemination as well as developing and modifying dissemination systems ('Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination to user and/or subject matter clients.'). They also review and approve dissemination-related parameters and are involved in the adaptation and presentation of data to a range of audiences.

Future GSBPM expectation: The future state emphasizes digital-first, metadata-rich, and automated delivery and promotion of products, requiring that dissemination strategies be integrated with AI-driven analytics, targeted by user segments, and optimized through continuous metrics-driven feedback loops.

Role evolution: The EC-05 will become responsible for aligning divisional dissemination policies and activation strategies with these automated digital tools, guiding how products are made machine-actionable and discoverable outside traditional platforms. They will need to shape how metadata is structured, ensure products are integrated with APIs, monitor real-time engagement, and use those insights to continuously improve strategies. Policy-making and advisement will increasingly focus on digital discoverability, not only human communication effectiveness.

Capability implication: Critical capabilities will now include knowledge of digital products’ lifecycle within open data ecosystems, advanced understanding of structured metadata and interoperability standards, fluent use of engagement dashboards/analytics to measure and improve digital reach, and the capacity to design governance for machine-driven promotions linked to trust, transparency, and outcome measurement.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Provide user support
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The Production and Dissemination Specialist (EC-05) 'provides subject-matter expertise and consultative services to users within and outside STC' and is responsible for 'interpreting the results of tests, procedural investigations and feasibility studies to produce data bases and data retrieval packages...' User support responsibilities are executed in the context of explaining complex data concepts, devising solutions for ad-hoc statistical information requests, and managing the dissemination of statistical information using various guidelines and formats.

Future GSBPM expectation: This function must evolve to support a user population increasingly comprised of power users and automated systems (e.g., via APIs, AI consumption). The support provided will be less about direct user education and more about ensuring data and systems are comprehensively documented, discoverable, interoperable, and accessible for advanced, programmatic use cases. Troubleshooting, guidance, and enablement will primarily be embedded within digital channels and self-service ecosystems, with person-to-person support for highly complex or novel scenarios.

Role evolution: The specialist will play a critical role in curating and maintaining rich metadata, ensuring the 'shape' of data products anticipates technical and analytical user needs, and collaborating with platform, IT, and metadata teams to improve user enablement and issue resolution. The scope of support expands to include not only helping users find and use data but also optimizing digital platforms for machine-actionable access and contributing to the design of digital feedback mechanisms and automated support content.

Capability implication: The EC-05 Specialist must increasingly command expertise in production metadata, understand modern API interfaces and their documentation needs, and work with analytics from user platforms to inform improvements. They will also need to understand programmatic consumption patterns and be able to represent user perspectives (including those of advanced or automated agents) in conversations about platform or product evolution.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Gather evaluation inputs
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist coordinates, controls, and leads teams in data manipulation, storage and retrieval, develops guidelines for processing systems, and conducts reviews and approvals for processing parameters, systems, and data evaluations. The specialist also provides expert consultation on statistical methods, develops guidelines for evaluation and testing, and analyzes the effectiveness of processing systems. Future GSBPM expectation: As evaluation inputs are collected by system design and monitored through automated dashboards, the EC-05 specialist’s focus will shift from overseeing manual manipulation, compilation, and review to leading the creation and configuration of automated, embedded evaluation tools, ensuring the accuracy, coverage, and relevance of system-generated evaluation indicators, and interpreting their outputs for ongoing program quality and improvement. Role evolution: The specialist will be more engaged with the ongoing configuration of system instrumentation, determining and refining the metrics that should populate dashboard and automated reports, and intervening in cases of exception or when new evaluation approaches are needed. Capability implication: Deeper understanding of statistical process instrumentation, the architecture of automated evaluation systems, and the effective use of machine-generated quality indicators for management and improvement will be required.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Conduct evaluation
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist leads and approves evaluation of processing systems, develops guidelines for design, evaluation and testing, and is responsible for reviewing and recommending modifications for quality and compatibility, as seen in 'Develops guidelines for the design, evaluation and testing of processing systems,' 'Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters,' and 'Research and analysis are required to evaluate the effectiveness of processing systems.' This includes approving process improvements and ensuring alignment with quality and output goals. 

Future GSBPM expectation: Evaluation processes will be built into the production workflow and automated via dashboards providing real-time quality signals and benchmarking, replacing much of the episodic, after-the-fact evaluation work described.

Role evolution: The EC-05 will shift from leadership over periodic system/process evaluations and extensive reporting toward a more dynamic, ongoing oversight of real-time, automated evaluation outputs, ensuring program responsiveness to alerts and system flags. The specialist will also need to ensure that recommendations for change are tracked and resolved in shorter, more focused increments, as well as ensuring data pipelines emit evaluation-ready metrics by default. Documentation duties will move from broad narrative reports to concise dashboard and issue resolution-based recordkeeping.

Capability implication: This heightens the importance of understanding how to leverage automated system reporting, real-time workflow management, and how to embed and interpret continuous quality and performance information into operational decisions.

Production and Dissemination Specialist.title: Agree an action plan
Production and Dissemination Specialist.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist currently defines project objectives, prepares work plans, outlines approaches, timeframes, and resources, and develops guidelines for evaluation and modification of processing systems (‘Defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources’; ‘Develops guidelines for the design, evaluation and testing of processing systems and applications and recommends modifications and improvements to existing procedures’). This includes responsibility for reviewing and approving changes and managing teams executing statistical activities.
Future GSBPM expectation: The future state elevates the necessity for rapidly formulated, transparent, and trackable action plans that support automated and modular infrastructures. Action plans now require explicit monitoring of execution and impact, iterative recalibration, and integration into digital platforms for automated assignment and follow-through.
Role evolution: The EC-05 Specialist’s work will evolve from episodic planning, approval, and review—potentially in less formalized or slower cycles—to developing and operationalizing action plans that must be standardized, digitally traced, rapidly executed, accountable, and responsive to ongoing feedback. The Specialist will have to embed monitoring criteria and mechanisms for impact assessment, oversee near-real-time progress, and be able to intervene or adjust plans in a disciplined and transparent fashion—supporting agile, outcome-driven operations over top-down or hierarchical approaches.
Capability implication: This change elevates the importance of knowledge in digital workflow orchestration, process automation tracking, and agile operational governance. The Specialist will need a much deeper facility with transparent, auditable process management, impact-driven analysis, and the integration of feedback loops related to automated and AI-enabled systems.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Identify needs
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: Current responsibility: The 'Head, Production and Dissemination' (EC-06) plans and implements long-term program strategies, develops policies, assesses program requirements, and reviews the conceptual framework for statistical programs (e.g., 'Prepares program proposals outlining options and recommendations on the statistical framework, strategies, resource implications and impact of new or modified statistical programs.'). The position is responsible for determining data acquisition methods, assessing trends, and integrating data from various sources, often including data not originally collected for current purposes. Future GSBPM expectation: The revised 'Identify needs' phase now serves as a strategic enterprise-wide gatekeeper, with a proactive obligation to scan all data assets for reusability, assess operational feasibility of new collections, and apply dynamic cost/timeliness/risk trade-offs. This function is essential to realizing StatCan2030’s objectives for efficiency, digital enablement, and resource optimization. Role evolution: This leadership role will shift toward enforcing digital-first, cross-program data asset utilization and implementing standardized needs identification procedures supported by digital platforms (e.g., data inventories, risk/cost tracking tools). EC-06 incumbents must drive this culture change and ensure that proposals for new projects include thorough, auditable documentation of needs assessment, alternative data explorations, and automation-readiness. They will increasingly participate in resource trade-off decisions, digital workflow alignment, and must build and reinforce mechanisms for early, digitally-enabled stakeholder engagement. Capability implication: This elevates the importance of strategic data asset management expertise, awareness of digital and AI technologies for discovery and automation, advanced understanding of cost/risk frameworks, and the ability to champion cross-organizational change toward digital, sustainable statistical production.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Consult and confirm needs
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination, plans and implements strategies for statistical programs, prepares program proposals, develops policies and guidelines, and provides expert advisory and consultative services to users. The position involves 'investigating client requirements for statistical information and determining the capacity and ability of existing or modified systems to meet these requirements,' and requires knowledge of key client department policies to identify and respond to information needs. The current approach supports both custom development and adaption of existing methods/products in response to evolving client demand, often in a consultative, iterative fashion.

Future GSBPM expectation: In the future-state, program launch and needs confirmation become highly evidence-driven, prioritizing reuse, automation, and cost efficiency. Strategy and program decisions will require explicit resource alignment and justification for any new data collection, with consultations underpinned by shared, transparent platforms tracking needs, commitments, and trade-off decisions. The role expands into stewardship of the consultation ecosystem: ensuring staff leverage digital tools, that process cycles are short and trackable, and that agency prioritization (what gets built) is transparent and defensible. Decision-logging and metadata-driven alignment are integral parts of this expectation.

Role evolution: The Head’s responsibilities will move toward embedding real-time consultation support mechanisms, monitoring and guiding the adoption of digital platforms for needs consultation, and defining the boundary conditions for when new collections are justified. Leadership will shift away from supporting exploratory program expansions to enforcing a rigorous structure of reuse-first, feasibility-driven, and transparently documented consultations. Accountability will include tracking consultation timelines, overseeing trade-off and cost-benefit deliberations, and ensuring continuous process improvement through feedback loops captured in shared tools.

Capability implication: This creates a heightened need for expertise in digital product/platform development for stakeholder consultation, oversight of automated and AI-augmented consultation workflows, advanced resource optimization, and knowledge of performance analytics for process cycles (timeliness, reuse rates, rejection/acceptance of new data collection proposals). Deep understanding of policy, strategic prioritization, and the mechanisms for effective, transparent trade-off discussions will be necessary, as well as change management proficiency to shepherd the workforce through these operational and cultural shifts.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Establish output objectives
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination is responsible for planning and implementing long-term strategies for statistical programs, developing and recommending frameworks, policies, and guidelines, and preparing program proposals outlining statistical frameworks, strategies, and resource implications ('Prepares program proposals outlining options and recommendations on the statistical framework, strategies, resource implications and impact of new or modified statistical programs.'). The Head also defines the methods and practices for data acquisition, production, and dissemination, and manages the evaluation of new data sources and systems for their feasibility and program impact.

Future GSBPM expectation: The future-state output objective establishment process is considerably redefined: it mandates that objectives prioritize asset reuse, automation-readiness, digital and resource efficiency, and interoperability by default, with demonstrable justification for any custom/manual or survey-first approaches. Approval for output objectives thus shifts toward an investment-style gate, tightly linked to enterprise architecture, automation pipelines, and digital resource limitations.

Role evolution: The EC-06 will now need to ensure all program and project proposals systematically demonstrate adherence to reuse, automation, and interoperability gates before advancing, integrating enterprise architecture and IT conversations into the earliest scoping and objective-setting decisions. This role will lead in formalizing processes and criteria for objective acceptance, establishing requirements for automation, and enforcing resource and feasibility discipline. It will require more structured collaboration across program, subject-matter, IT, and data governance leads to present business cases for any non-standard output.

Capability implication: The change elevates the importance of strategic data asset stewardship, deep alignment with enterprise IT and automation standards, and the capability to analyze, synthesize, and communicate cost-benefit and digital feasibility arguments at the program acceptance stage. The Head must also be able to balance statistical relevance with digital architecture constraints, and audit or establish processes for evaluating output proposals against agency-wide, automation-first priorities.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Identify concepts
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-06 oversees the development and implementation of divisional statistical programs, establishes concepts and definitions, manages the integration of multi-source data, and is responsible for resolving compatibility issues and developing policies and guidelines. The position also regularly assesses the need for modification or adaptation of conceptual frameworks across programs, often building ground-up justifications based on program or user-driven requirements.

Future GSBPM expectation: The future state expects EC-06 leaders to champion the adoption of automated, metadata-based concept identification systems, ensure divisional alignment with enterprise data assets and FAIR principles, and arbitrate prioritization and exception cases at a cross-divisional or enterprise level. Leaders are accountable for steering the transition from manual to system-curated conceptual frameworks and ensuring scalable, reusable outputs for digital integration.

Role evolution: The EC-06 role evolves from managing isolated program-level conceptual frameworks to leading multi-domain harmonization, setting policies that guide the arbitration of AI-suggested concepts, and driving the adoption of enterprise metadata practices. Leadership responsibilities now encompass orchestrating rapid arbitration processes, justifying deviations from standardized concepts, and integrating outputs with end-to-end automation.

Capability implication: This creates greater reliance on knowledge of enterprise architecture, metadata management, digital governance (e.g., FAIR principles), and the ability to facilitate organizational change toward systemic, automated workflows for concept identification.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Check data availability and suitability
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination is responsible for preparing program proposals on statistical frameworks, developing policies, procedures, and guidelines for system development, and determining the methods and practices for data acquisition, production, and dissemination. The role entails evaluating the suitability of new and emerging data sources, reviewing conceptual frameworks, integrating data from a variety of sources (e.g., financial statements, tax files, administrative sources, surveys), and ensuring legislative requirements (including confidentiality, privacy, and data access) are met. The work description emphasizes 'assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and ... identifies the availability and reliability of new data sources to evaluate the suitability of new hardware and software and to determine the short and long term program impact and benefits.'

Future GSBPM expectation: The future state outlines a shift to automated, AI-enabled assessments for data availability and suitability, emphasizing a standard, technology-driven prioritization of existing internal and alternative data holdings before considering new surveys. Human expertise is redirected to overseeing automation, resolving complex legal and risk cases, and managing data partnerships. There is a new expectation for transparent, evidence-based justification for survey proposals, in-depth legal/ethical vetting related to third-party or alternative data, and ongoing curation of metadata used for automated discovery.

Role evolution: This role will move from overseeing manual and reactive reviews of data availability to designing and governing processes for automated, systematized, and metadata-driven discovery and assessment of data sources. Decision-making will intensify around legal, ethical, and quality oversight for automated systems, and strategic management of partner relationships and access negotiations (especially with non-traditional and private data holders). The EC-06 will set policies for the use of AI-powered assessment tools, lead in evolving frameworks for data suitability, and arbitrate complex suitability, confidentiality, and legislative edge cases flagged by automation.

Capability implication: Deep contextual and operational knowledge will remain critical but now must extend to evaluating and overseeing AI-driven data discovery, machine-actionable metadata infrastructure, privacy-by-design workflow automation, and risk/impact assessment frameworks. Understanding of dynamic legal and contractual obligations for externally-held data, along with capability in change management for process modernization and partnership negotiation, becomes much more important in the future operating model.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Design outputs and dissemination
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head plans and implements long-term strategies for development, enhancement, and operation of statistical programs, certifies output quality, establishes policies/procedures for dissemination and confidentiality, and oversees conceptual frameworks and integration with external programs. The role's mandate specifically references reviewing and recommending applications of new technologies and methods in mass data processing, but presently this is largely oriented around traditional or semi-automated legacy systems and output modalities.
Future GSBPM expectation: StatCan2030 redefines dissemination as foundational to the entire statistical system, with outputs needing to be automated, metadata- and API-driven, interoperable, discoverable, and available for both human and machine consumption. This strategic shift requires senior program leads to drive not only compliance with such standards, but also systemic transformation—embedding machine-actionable thinking and modularity into design, ensuring robust confidentiality and access rules, and guaranteeing alignment with broader organizational IT and metadata architectures.
Role evolution: The Head must move from overseeing programs which produce human-focused outputs and upgrades, to managing the transition to and operation of standardized, automated dissemination pipelines, including specification, procurement, and evaluation of interoperable platforms. Leadership responsibilities expand to include stewardship of data discoverability, API access, and secure, traceable platforms enabling both human and automated usage. The Head is increasingly accountable for ensuring that the unit delivers not just statistical products, but also trusted, reusable, and extensible dissemination services as a product/platform owner.
Capability implication: This creates a need for in-depth understanding of machine-actionable design, API and automation strategy, advanced metadata architecture, and trust-by-design/ethical release practices at scale. Broader literacy in interoperability frameworks, platform/product management, and the integration of confidentiality/data ethics into technical design becomes imperative. The Head becomes central to driving a product-oriented, scalable approach to data dissemination and leading workforce transformation to support this model.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Design variables
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The Head manages the strategy, development, implementation, and operation of new and modified statistical systems, defines frameworks and guidelines for systems/processes, and provides high-level advisory services regarding the development and use of data structures. Evidence: 'Plans and implements long term strategies', 'Develops policies, guidelines, instructions and procedures for the development, use and evaluation of systems and processes', and 'Reviews the conceptual framework of existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaption.'

Future GSBPM expectation: At future-state, variable design is strategic and foundational, requiring active leadership in establishing and maintaining enterprise-wide, machine-actionable variable and metadata standards. Heads will need to ensure all divisional programs and systems adhere to centralized frameworks, that governance and stewardship of variable assets are robust, and that their area is future-proofed for automation and AI readiness.

Role evolution: The Head’s responsibility for setting frameworks, policies, and standards now encompasses leading the adoption of metadata-rich, interoperability-first cultures and ensuring that system and program designs enable seamless registration, versioning, and reuse of variables across the enterprise. They will be called upon to champion the operational shift, mediate requirements with emerging standards, and drive the division’s engagement in cross-program governance. Decision-making extends to the prioritization and resourcing of metadata stewardship and the integration of new tools and processes that embody FAIR principles.

Capability implication: This intensifies the need for advanced knowledge in enterprise metadata governance, semantic interoperability, the organizational impacts of automation, and strategic change management in statistico-technical environments. Familiarity with the operational, strategic, and technological aspects of enterprise-wide variable standardization and stewardship is essential.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Design collection
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination is accountable for long-term planning, establishing policies, guiding strategy and governance for statistical program systems—'Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of divisional statistical programs', 'Develops policies, guidelines, instructions and procedures for the development, use and evaluation of systems and processes', and 'Reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results.' The role deeply influences framework design, system integration, and policy for collection and dissemination.

Future GSBPM expectation: StatCan2030 requires EC-06 roles to champion a fundamental transformation from bespoke, division-specific collection strategies to modular, interoperable, metadata-driven, and highly automated enterprise frameworks. EC-06s will oversee the transition from labor-intensive survey design to validating and improving AI-based, data-source-first pipelines, and ensuring their units comply with updated transparency, audit, and ethical oversight mandates, while maintaining efficiency and quality.

Role evolution: Rather than guiding incremental improvements in legacy program designs, EC-06s must architect and enforce adoption of modular, standardized systems, facilitate cross-divisional integration of collection frameworks, and implement enterprise-wide monitoring, auditability, and exception management processes for AI automation in the design collection phase. Responsibility expands to include oversight of AI model validation, configuration of guardrails for automation, and ensuring systems-level interoperability. Their authority and accountability extend beyond their unit to the broader operational ecosystem, with heightened stakes for compliance, scalability, and real-time responsiveness.

Capability implication: They will need advanced knowledge of modular system architecture, AI automation governance, metadata management, and cross-system interoperability. Expertise in leading organizational change, implementing audit trails for automated decisions, and upholding ethical and transparency requirements in a highly automated environment becomes essential.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Design frame and sample
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination oversees long-term strategies and program frameworks for statistical programs, certifies program quality, and establishes policies for data acquisition and production, which have included overseeing the methodological foundations underpinning manual or semi-automated sample and frame design. They are responsible for 'determining the methods, concepts, techniques and practices to be applied' and 'reviewing the conceptual framework of existing statistical programs,' including those that determine how populations are framed and samples are drawn. Future GSBPM expectation: The shift to fully automated, AI-orchestrated sampling pipelines demands that program heads define strategy and policies for the integration of AI-enabled selection, establish oversight mechanisms for systemized, modular, interoperable process automation, and handle division-wide exceptions, ethical considerations, and quality assurance in an environment where surveys are a last—rather than default—resort. Role evolution: The Head's task will change from guiding improvements to manual systems and setting traditional methodological policies to setting parameters for automated logic, overseeing system performance and ethical/quality implications of AI-driven sampling, and resolving high-impact exceptions or failures in automated selection. Capability implication: This requires advanced capability in understanding the intersection of statistical methodology, automated system design, AI, and governance/ethics frameworks for automation, as well as the ability to guide staff in integrating alternative data into operational sampling logic and ensure compliance with national and international metadata and interoperability standards.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Design processing and analysis
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination, sets divisional strategy for system design, manages the development and implementation of statistical processing and dissemination systems, defines specifications for large-scale processing projects, and is responsible for expert and strategic advisory on new methods and technologies in mass data processing. This role requires setting policies, certifying quality, and ensuring that systems and data processes are compliant, interoperable, and fit for purpose across a range of statistical programs. Future GSBPM expectation: In future, strategy and oversight must guarantee all design and development is modular, automation-ready, and based on standardized, reusable logic—enforcing system-wide adoption of FAIR, metadata-driven approaches, validation via automation, and robust version-control and auditability by default. The expectation is that leaders ensure all process designs are interoperable, machine-actionable, auditable, and align with organization-wide standards and governance for automation and responsible AI. Role evolution: The EC-06 will need to shift resource planning, policy-setting, and system oversight from managing bespoke system design and legacy process integration toward building the organizational and technical scaffolding for end-to-end standardization, modularity, and automation. This means championing new governance, steering major change management, and ensuring teams translate business requirements into platform-compatible, automation-ready designs. Capability implication: Capabilities in digital transformation leadership, modular and metadata-driven enterprise design, responsible automation governance, implementation of cross-domain standards, and auditable, interoperable process architecture will become pivotal. Advanced knowledge in orchestrating change, maintaining enterprise-wide versioning, and ensuring the operationalization of automated, ethics-ready, and reproducible analytical environments is essential.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Design production systems and workflows
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The 'Head, Production and Dissemination' (EC-06) 'plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of divisional statistical programs,' 'defines, coordinates and evaluates the cost of statistical system development work,' 'plans and controls the development and implementation of new or modified statistical systems,' and 'manages a unit and project teams involved in systems design.' This means the Head is accountable for strategic system planning and resourcing, policy and guideline development, and approval of technical and operational direction for divisional workflows.

Future GSBPM expectation: The future state expects system and workflow design to be an enterprise concern, not strictly divisional, emphasizing orchestration across programs, automation, interoperable modules, and metadata-driven governance, enforced through agile, standardized frameworks and closer alignment with enterprise IT/business platforms. Strategic leadership is needed to drive adoption of open standards and event-driven design, deploying solutions that facilitate self-service development while maintaining robust governance and auditability.

Role evolution: The EC-06 Head will need to drive and champion the transition from custom, divisional system builds to enterprisewide, reusable platforms and solutions. The role’s strategy and oversight duties expand to include the adoption and operationalization of enterprise architecture, opening divisional activities to greater cross-program standardization and alignment. The Head will become key in shaping governance guardrails, ensuring staff at all levels understand and embody modular and automated design principles, and in coordinating adaptation to emerging automation and AI-enabled approaches.

Capability implication: Strategic and operational expertise in modular, enterprise-scale workflow frameworks; deep understanding of standards-based, metadata-driven automation; and the ability to lead change management across technical and subject-matter teams become essential. The Head must have knowledge of the risks, compliance, and governance challenges introduced by automation and self-service architectures, and a sophisticated understanding of how to incentivize and monitor adoption of new architectural patterns and frameworks department-wide.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Reuse or build collection instruments
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination is accountable for strategic planning, program development, and the implementation of large-scale statistical systems and processes. The head manages financial and human resources, develops policies and procedures for data collection and processing, and assesses system development needs in light of new trends and requirements. Oversight includes evaluating the suitability of new hardware/software, conceptual framework revisions, and system quality review.
Future GSBPM expectation: The entire practice of instrument construction is refactored to emphasize automated, standards-driven modularity, low-code/no-code tools, deep metadata integration, and 'surveys as a last resort.' The Head will no longer be approving highly customized projects or solutions, but is instead responsible for the governance and enablement of self-service development, platform and metadata architecture, compliance to security/quality privacy standards, and rapid, scalable deployment of tools by a broader base of (non-IT) staff.
Role evolution: The incumbent will need to shift focus toward governance and architectural stewardship of enterprise instrument platforms, policy-setting for modular and AI-enabled workflows, and ensuring organizational capability to support decentralized/self-service instrument creation under strict guardrails. The Head must orchestrate the architectural integration of collection instruments into end-to-end automated pipelines and lead organizational adaptation to rapid cycles of instrument reuse and platform-based innovation.
Capability implication: This elevates the importance of advanced platform architecture knowledge, metadata governance, digital compliance/audit understanding, and the ability to lead both cultural and technological change toward sustainable automation and interoperability in collection instrument development and deployment.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination sets strategy, plans and controls the development and operation of statistical systems, and is responsible for decisions about methodologies, frameworks, and technologies. The position defines long-term strategies and quality standards ('Establishes policies and procedures for... computer systems, equipment, databases and files' and 'Reviews trends and developments in data processing concepts, methods and techniques in order to present options and recommendations').

Future GSBPM expectation: The strategic focus moves to mandating modularity, reuse, AI/automation, and standardized platforms. This includes organization-wide governance of interoperable components, compliance with rigorous audit and reproducibility standards, and oversight of the democratization of development through low-code platforms extending to business areas.

Role evolution: The EC-06 must redefine system development and operational quality strategies, shifting oversight from managing bespoke software and manual customizations to implementing policies, standards, and organizational practices that support composable module libraries, robust governance, and secure, rapid deployment at scale. The position will be central in championing and ensuring upskilling, transparent audit trails, and pipeline accountability across a broader, more decentralized base of solution developers.

Capability implication: Deep knowledge of governance frameworks for modular and AI-powered platforms, auditability best practices, and the management of change in environments leveraging low-code/no-code by business users become paramount, far surpassing current requirements for traditional bespoke system management.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Reuse or build dissemination components
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head manages strategic planning, system development, and operational delivery for the division’s production and dissemination functions, including 'plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of divisional statistical programs,' develops policies and guidelines for system use and evaluation, and authorizes expenditures and contracts for system acquisition and maintenance. The Head certifies 'the overall quality and completeness of program results' and ensures systems are compatible with departmental priorities and policies. Future GSBPM expectation: With the future requirement that all dissemination use standardized, reusable, and centrally-governed components, the Head will be expected to align strategic vision, resource management, and policy development with this high level of technical and operational standardization. Decisions regarding new projects, technology adoption, and allocation of resources will need to account for the necessity to use enterprise platforms and avoid custom, siloed solutions. Role evolution: The Head’s leadership and decision-making will transform to prioritize adoption, integration, and continuous improvement within the enterprise’s modular, reusable dissemination ecosystem, including guiding teams in capability shifts and ensuring compliance with strict platform and governance standards. The Head will have to ensure that divisional strategies, quality assurance measures, and advisory functions fully reflect the new realities—specifically, automation, instant machine/human-readiness, and AI-driven dissemination needs. Capability implication: Advanced architectural literacy in enterprise platforms, comprehensive understanding of modular data and solution governance, and strategic capacity to manage talent, procurement, and innovation within the constraints and opportunities of a centrally-managed, standardized dissemination architecture become critical—and override prior assumptions about local customization or independent development.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Configure workflows
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination leads in planning and implementing statistical programs and systems, develops policies and guidelines for statistical system development, and manages teams responsible for designing and operating statistical processes. The position requires advanced knowledge of systems analysis and design, and assesses the suitability of emerging technologies for division-wide solutions ('Develops policies, guidelines, instructions and procedures for the development, use and evaluation of systems and processes.') and ('Reviews trends and developments in data processing concepts, methods and techniques in order to present options and recommendations to management on the use and application of new technology...').

Future GSBPM expectation: Leadership in workflow configuration shifts to overseeing and ensuring the adoption and governance of standardized, modular, automated enterprise workflow platforms. The EC-06 is expected to drive and ensure compliance with these new ways of working—balancing empowered business-line configuration with secure, reproducible, and auditable workflows. They must establish appropriate structures and oversight for orchestration, version control, and platform governance, rather than managing disparate systems and manual workarounds.

Role evolution: The EC-06's strategic and governance responsibilities will pivot to policy-making and oversight concerning the implementation of standardized orchestration and automation. This includes championing and monitoring adherence to enterprise workflow standards, supporting workforce transformation towards business-led configuration using low-code/no-code platforms, setting expectations for workflow version control and auditability, and ensuring IT and business area collaboration in configuring and maintaining reusable modules.

Capability implication: High-level capability in change management for digital modernization, and in the strategic leadership of workflow automation platforms, governance, transparency, and platform-enabled workforce transformation, now becomes essential. Applied leadership in standardization, configuration discipline, and in the interface between business empowerment and IT guardrails is crucial.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Test production systems
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination, sets strategies and guidelines for developing and operating statistical systems, defines and evaluates system development work, develops policies on security and data protection, and reviews overall system and program quality. Evidence: 'Develops policies, guidelines, instructions and procedures for the development, use and evaluation of systems and processes.' and 'Establishes policies and procedures for the security and confidentiality of data and the maintenance and protection of computer systems, equipment, databases and files.'
Future GSBPM expectation: The future state places a premium on enterprise-wide, standardized, automated testing practices encompassing not only technical validation but also compliance with cross-cutting controls (e.g., security, privacy, FAIR, audit). Heads will be accountable for the systemic readiness of their production systems, ensuring programmatic adherence to continuous, automated quality and governance checks, and supporting business-area attestation and automated approval workflows.
Role evolution: The Head’s responsibilities extend to oversight of automated, integrated test and compliance frameworks, ensuring divisional adoption of standardized protocols and governance requirements. This includes driving culture and process changes, embedding compliance and reproducibility in operations, assuring readiness for audit and attestation, and balancing program innovation with enterprise guardrails.
Capability implication: Stronger proficiency in operationalizing compliance at scale, leading the implementation of automated controls, understanding integration between program-specific and enterprise platform capabilities, and cultivating a workforce attuned to continuous and accountable system testing will be critical.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Test statistical business process
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The Head, Production and Dissemination (EC-06) plans and controls statistical system development and operation, reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results, and develops policies and guidelines for the development, use, and evaluation of systems and processes. The role includes the oversight of system specification definition, as well as process and production guideline setting for development work. Evidence: 'Reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results.' and 'Develops policies, guidelines, instructions and procedures for the development, use and evaluation of systems and processes.'
Future GSBPM expectation: The modernization of GSBPM phase 3.6 means that management must ensure a thorough and transparent testing regime for statistical business processes, with mechanisms for early detection and mitigation of risks across the workflow, and clear lines of accountability for test coverage and results.
Role evolution: The EC-06 will therefore need to not just oversee testing in terms of policy, but provide strategic leadership and governance around testing practices, resource prioritization for process validation, and ensure adoption of modern, robust testing strategies department-wide. Their involvement will be critical in aligning testing practices with departmental standards for quality, innovation, and system integration.
Capability implication: This demands advanced contextual understanding of process quality assurance, process change and risk management, and the strategic integration of testing as a core part of production modernization—ensuring both compliance and innovation, and enabling a culture of continuous improvement in process testing.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Finalise production systems
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: 1. Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination plans and oversees development, enhancement, and operation of divisional production systems, including establishing policies, ensuring system security and confidentiality, and implementing production processes ('Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of divisional statistical programs,' 'Establishes policies and procedures for the security and confidentiality of data and the maintenance and protection of computer systems...'). They manage the integration of new technologies, direct team/contractor resources, and provide department-wide knowledge transfer and expertise. 2. Future GSBPM expectation: The future state means that all finalised production systems must be automated, modular, and compliant with enterprise, governance, and FAIR standards. The process features ongoing operationalization, monitoring, real-time enablement, extensive documentation and training, and shared ownership across a more diverse set of users. There is also an institutional shift toward self-service, reproducibility, and rapid, iterative deployment. 3. Role evolution: The Head will move from managing legacy linear system hand-offs to implementing policies and governance for end-to-end automated, FAIR-compliant, and AI-enabled pipelines. The Head will be responsible for policies and procedures that enable self-service, cross-disciplinary operational responsibility, and continuous enablement. The role must now guarantee institutional compliance, proper documentation and training frameworks for varied audiences, and create a culture of ongoing monitoring and agility. 4. Capability implication: This will place greater emphasis on deep understanding of modular/platform architectures, operational governance, attestation and compliance practices, policy setting for user enablement, FAIR principles, and security requirements. The Head must ensure organizational readiness for active, distributed ownership of finalised production systems, and foster adaptive, transparent processes for both technical and non-technical user communities.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Create frame and select sample – Future-State Implications
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination, is accountable for strategic planning and operational implementation of statistical programs, including defining system and process specifications, developing policies and guidelines, and certifying quality of results. The role manages units responsible for the development of statistical systems and production environments. The work includes researching trends in data processing, evaluating emerging concepts and technologies, and recommending systemic changes to management.

Future GSBPM expectation: Under the new paradigm, the Head will be responsible for ensuring their programs participate in, and benefit from, the agency-wide automated and AI-enabled sampling and frame modules. Oversight, auditability, methodological governance, and facilitating cross-program harmonization are now strategic imperatives. Adapting policy and operational frameworks to support survey minimization, automation, and methodological innovation will be expected. The role will also need to advocate for and guide methodological R&D and organizational change associated with this shift.

Role evolution: The Head will shift from managing manual and legacy system development and operational processes to leading transformation towards platform-based, automated statistical production. They will drive the integration and harmonization of register-based and alternative data sources, enabling minimal manual intervention and providing oversight for exception management, quality assurance, innovation, and continuous improvement of automated processes.

Capability implication: Deep understanding of agency-wide automation strategies, platform-based frame and sampling systems, and their governance, as well as advanced methodological acumen around leveraging AI and auxiliary data, become crucial. Leadership of cross-program operational optimization becomes a central responsibility, as does managing the organizational change required to shift traditional teams to future-facing oversight and exception-handling roles.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Set up collection
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination sets long-term strategic direction for system development and enhancement, establishes policies and guidelines for statistical program systems, manages resources for system design and development, and ensures data quality, security, and compliance ('Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of divisional statistical programs.' and 'Develops policies, guidelines, instructions and procedures for the development, use and evaluation of systems and processes.'). They are also charged with reviewing new technology and assessing its impact on production, managing large teams, and overseeing complex integration or quality frameworks. 
Future GSBPM expectation: Automated, modular, and AI-assisted collection set-up becomes standardized across the organization. Strategic priorities demand reduced manual, bespoke work and a stronger oversight and governance focus, especially in areas of automation, risk, exception management, rapid scaling, and ethical/secure use of new technologies. Heads must shift resources from legacy process management to forward-looking platform governance and cross-program integration, while ensuring new set-up methods meet portfolio/program needs and compliance. 
Role evolution: The Head's work will evolve toward setting policy and governance structures for automated collection ecosystems, risk, bias, and AI logic monitoring, determining enterprise readiness for rapid digital pivots (such as quickly onboarding new digital or administrative data sources), and assuring cross-divisional alignment on standardized practices. Resource allocation, workforce planning, and stakeholder management must reflect the shift away from routine operational tasks toward functions centered in system oversight, compliance, and adaptation to emergent automation challenges. 
Capability implication: Enterprise-level understanding of platform automation, AI model validation as it pertains to collection and integration, governance for privacy/security/ethics in systematized environments, and change leadership to guide the workforce transition to automation-centric processes become critically important.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Run collection
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-06 'Head, Production and Dissemination' sets division-level strategies for program development and operations, oversees the implementation of new statistical systems, manages the integration of data from diverse sources, and leads organizational response to operational and technological trends ('Plans and implements long term strategies [...] for the development, enhancement and operation of divisional statistical programs.'; 'Reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results.'). The incumbent is accountable for policy, procedure, and technological direction in all aspects of production and dissemination, including mass data capture, and interfaces with external stakeholders and system suppliers.

Future GSBPM expectation: The future state renders mass manual collection unsustainable, calls for strategic workforce and workflow re-alignment around systems integration, automation, and paradata-driven quality management. The division lead must architect an environment where human effort targets strategic exceptions, process improvement, and stakeholder relationship escalation, as opposed to routine collection logistics. The operational management of digital acquisition platforms and oversight of system performance at enterprise scale become central.

Role evolution: The EC-06's leadership pivots to the transformation of business processes, workforce structure, and technical ecosystem towards AI-enabled, automated, and event-driven data collection. This encompasses not only change management for staff roles but also strategic direction for technology investments, partnerships for administrative and alternative data sharing, and stewardship of new policies for digital process monitoring, exception handling, and stakeholder engagement. Decision authority increasingly relies on evaluating the performance and resilience of complex digital collection architectures and enforcing a rapid-response capability for exceptions or quality assurance interventions where automation is insufficient.

Capability implication: Strategic, program-level understanding of automated collection system architecture, advanced knowledge of integrated data acquisition strategies, digital process monitoring and organizational change levers, and the ability to link evolving technical and operational requirements with legislative, policy, and stakeholder management considerations become critical for continued divisional success.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Finalise collection
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification:
Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head plans, implements, and manages divisional strategies for statistical databases, systems, and processes, establishes policies for the development and safeguarding of systems, and leads system integration and modernization initiatives ('Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of divisional statistical programs.'; 'Establishes policies and procedures for the security and confidentiality of data and the maintenance and protection of computer systems, equipment, databases and files.'). The role currently manages both manual and system-based approaches to data/collateral archiving, version control, and security/pseudonymization as explicit steps, often requiring procedural adaptation to new technology.
Future GSBPM expectation: The shift to automated, metadata-driven, and audit-ready finalization processes means that both governance and operational management must focus on orchestrated, standardized automation, and that policies, procedures, and risk management must address automated archiving, pseudonymization, versioning, and transparency by default. Manual, clerical, or idiosyncratic approaches are no longer standard; operational resilience hinges upon robust, enterprise-scale automation and continuous improvement based on paradata and pipeline analytics.
Role evolution: The Head's strategic responsibility pivots toward embedding and governing automation, metadata standards, version control, privacy, and exception-handling enterprise-wide. Oversight of production must emphasize continuous pipeline improvement, automation resilience, and integrity of data handoff to processing. Leadership will be increasingly technical and collaborative with IT/data engineering, focusing on the architectural reliability of interfaces, auditability, compliance, and operational risk management via automation—not human procedures. Policy direction will adjust to dictate automation standards and division of responsibilities between human experts and machine processes.
Capability implication: Deep organizational capability in automation governance, metadata and paradata strategy, machine-actionable compliance/audit frameworks, and operational risk in automated systems becomes critical. The Head must direct the evolution of production/dissemination strategies rooted in automation and continuous process improvement, setting and enforcing standards for data and metadata discoverability, security, version management, and exception oversight in an automated-first environment.

Head, Production and Dissemination.title: Integrate data
Head, Production and Dissemination.justification: Current responsibility: The EC-06 Head, Production and Dissemination oversees the strategic, operational, and quality aspects of divisional statistical programs, including planning and controlling statistical systems, evaluating their development, and taking responsibility for the integration of data from multiple sources into common frameworks (e.g., 'Reviews the conceptual framework of existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaption. Programs involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources...Source data have often been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts.'). Future GSBPM expectation: Automated, end-to-end, metadata-driven and auditable data integration platforms will underpin all integration work, with standardization across production lines and a need for robust governance and metadata stewardship at scale. Role evolution: The EC-06 must focus on strategic oversight of platform adoption, ensuring business alignment with automated data integration and orchestration environments, setting division-wide standards for modular pipeline use, championing metadata stewardship, and overseeing the management of integration exceptions or anomalies through automated monitoring infrastructures. Capability implication: The ability to strategically plan for and govern large-scale, automated, and interoperable integration environments—including setting organizational metadata and integration standards, ensuring auditability and compliance, and leading the adoption and scaling of new automated production paradigms—will be paramount compared to previously managing, modifying, or evaluating largely manual or semi-automated integration practices.
